models_evaluated: 12 individual LLMs (proprietary flagship, proprietary fast, open-source tiers)
three multi-agent LLM deliberative councils (four models each, with a designated chair)

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of multi-agent councils vs pooled individual LLMs on ophthalmology vignettes
links.effect: Councils outperformed pooled individual models in all tiers. Accuracy was 95.0% vs 90.8% (flagship), 96.0% vs 86.5% (fast), and 91.0% vs 83.2% (open-source).
links.quote: Accuracy improved for proprietary flagship (95.0% vs 90.8%; risk difference [RD]: 4.25 [95% CI: 0.45, 8.05]), proprietary fast (96.0% vs 86.5%; RD: 9.50 [5.31, 13.59]), and open-source councils (91.0% vs 83.2%; RD: 7.75 [4.17, 11.33]).

unlisted_practices: Multi-agent LLM deliberative councils (peer ranking and chair synthesis) to reduce harmful outputs and improve diagnostic accuracy

screen.reason: Evaluates multi-agent LLM deliberative councils (peer review and synthesis) versus single LLMs on ophthalmology clinical vignettes to reduce harm and improve diagnostic performance.
